name: line-segment
title: Line segment
tagline: Bare horizontal line with ordered labelled collinear points, ticks and occludable length braces; each length derived from the ratio + one given length. Not a numeric axis.
description: A single horizontal straight line segment carrying ordered, labelled collinear points (A–B–C…) that divide it into sub-segments, with a short vertical tick at each point, optional length braces on any span, and a "Not to scale" caption. The author writes the ordered points, the ratio of consecutive sub-segments, and ONE known length; every sub-segment length, span length, and the answer are derived (length = unit × ratio units spanned, the unit fixed by the given). Points are positioned proportional to the ratio (with a floor so extreme ratios stay legible) or spaced evenly for the bare exam figure. Point labels and measure values occlude independently to "?" — the "ABC is a straight line, AB:BC = m:n, find BC" hook — and any brace can be highlighted amber for the answer. This is deliberately NOT a number line: there is no numeric scale, no graduations, no zero — just a marked segment and the lengths of its parts.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever the teaching is "points lie on a straight line" and you divide the line in a ratio: "ABC is a straight line, AB:BC = 3:2, AC = 30 cm, find BC", points dividing a segment in a ratio, or simply showing three or more collinear points in order. Author the points in left-to-right order, the ratio over the consecutive sub-segments (length points − 1), and ONE given length (`given`) as the scale anchor — the model derives every other length. Common configurations: worked example — show the given and highlight the answer measure; occluded question — occlude the answer measure so its value reads "?" while the given stays visible; blank configuration — just points and ticks, no ratio or given (a bare "ABC is a straight line" stimulus). Spacing: "ratio" (default) draws the sub-segments proportional to their derived lengths — the honest ratio picture; "even" spaces the points equally — the schematic look of a bare exam figure that is genuinely not to scale. Do NOT reach for number/number-line here: it imposes a numeric axis, ticks-per-unit and a zero the source lacks; this model is the plain segment. Keep the same points and unit across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track one line. For algebraic parts (AB = 3x, BC = 2x) omit the given and use a measure `label` override on each span. Synonyms a teacher might use: straight line, collinear points, line segment, divide a line in a ratio, points on a line, AB:BC, partition a segment, ABC is a straight line, share a length.

points.description: The collinear points ON the line, in LEFT-TO-RIGHT order — this order defines their position order. Two points give one segment (A–B); three give two (A–B–C, B between A and C); and so on.

label.description: Display name shown beside the point, e.g. "A", "B", "P". Keep short (usually a single capital). Referenced by `given` and `measures` via from/to.

occlude.description: Render this point's label as "?" — a "name this point" hook. The tick stays visible. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this point's label — draw the eye to it. Default false.

ratio.description: The ratio of the consecutive sub-segments, left to right — one integer PER sub-segment, so its length must be (points − 1). AB:BC = 3:2 is [3, 2]; AB:BC:CD = 1:2:3 is [1, 2, 3]. Combined with `given` it derives every length. Omit for a bare configuration with no measurements (points and ticks only), or when every measure carries its own `label` override.

given.description: The ONE known length that fixes the scale — every other length derives from it. It is drawn as a length brace (so you never repeat it in `measures`). Needs `ratio` to derive the rest. Omit for a bare configuration or a fully label-overridden (algebraic) figure.

from.description: Label of the point the known length starts at (must be one of `points`).

to.description: Label of the point it ends at. `from`/`to` may be adjacent (a sub-segment, e.g. AB) OR span several points (e.g. AC, the total, or an interior span BD).

length.description: The known length in `unit`s, e.g. 30. Positive.

show.description: Draw the given's length brace and value. Default true. Set false to fix the scale without drawing this measurement.

highlight.description: Amber the given's brace and value. Default false.

measures.description: Additional length braces to draw on the line, each spanning `from`→`to` points. Every value is DERIVED (unit × ratio units spanned) unless a `label` override is given — you never author a derived length. This is where the answer segment lives (occlude it to pose the question, highlight it for the reveal).

from.description: Label of the point the measured span starts at.

to.description: Label of the point it ends at (right of `from`).

occlude.description: Render this measure's value as "?" — the "find this length" hook. The brace stays visible. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this measure's brace and value — answer emphasis. Default false.

label.description: Override the derived value with this exact string, e.g. "3x" for an algebraic part or a custom annotation. Bypasses derivation (like number-line's jump label) — use only when there is no numeric length to derive. Set "" to draw the brace with no value.

spacing.description: "ratio" (default): sub-segments are drawn proportional to their derived lengths (floored so an extreme ratio stays legible) — the honest ratio picture. "even": points are spaced equally regardless of length — the schematic look of a bare exam figure that is genuinely not to scale. Use "even" to reproduce a not-to-scale source figure; "ratio" when the proportion should be visible.

unit.description: Unit appended to every derived length, e.g. "cm", "m". Default "" (bare numbers). Keep consistent across a lesson.

showTicks.description: Draw the short vertical tick through the line at each point. Default true.

showNotToScale.description: Show the small "Not to scale" caption. Default true — the segment is schematic, never a ruler.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

examples.label: Blank marked line (configuration) — three collinear points, no measurements
Worked example — AB:BC = 3:2, AC = 30 cm, BC derived and highlighted
Occluded question — ABC straight line, AB:BC = 3:2, AC = 30 cm, find BC
Hard case — four points, interior span BD = 20 given, find AB (occluded + highlighted), even spacing
Algebraic parts — AB = 3x, BC = 2x, AC = 40 (label overrides, no given)
Given a part, find the total — AB = 12 cm, AB:BC = 3:2, AC highlighted, ratio spacing
